current_example.title: Example: Determining the Decoupling Substitution of a Linear System of Differential Equations

q-79673.name: Question 1
q-79673.problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$
q-79673.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Let v1=[10] and v2=[13] be eigenvectors of a matrix A that correspond to eigenvalues λ1=1 and λ2=−2, respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation x′(t)=Ax(t)?

a
x(t)=c1[30]et+c2[11]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
b
x(t)=c1[10]e−2t+c2[13]et,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[13]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[01]e−2t+c2[31]et,c1,c2∈R
e
x(t)=c1[11]et+c2[03]e−2t,c1,c2∈R
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form x′(t)=Ax(t), where A has two distinct eigenvalues λ1,λ2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1 and v2, the formula for the general solution is x(t)=c1v1eλ1t+c2v2eλ2t,c1,c2∈R.

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

x(t)=c1[10]et+c2[13]e−2t,c1,c2∈R.

q-79672.name: Question 2
q-79672.problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$
q-79672.worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Question 2
?

Let v1=[−21] and v2=[01] be eigenvectors of a matrix A that correspond to eigenvalues λ1=1 and λ2=−1, respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation x′(t)=Ax(t)?

a
x(t)=c1[1−2]e−t+c2[10]et,c1,c2∈R
b
x(t)=c1[21]et+c2[0−1]e−t,c1,c2∈R
c
x(t)=c1[−21]et+c2[01]e−t,c1,c2∈R
d
x(t)=c1[−21]e−t+c2[01]et,c1,c2∈R
e
x(t)=c1[01]et+c2[21]e−t,c1,c2∈R
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form x′(t)=Ax(t), where A has two distinct eigenvalues λ1,λ2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1 and v2, the formula for the general solution is x(t)=c1v1eλ1t+c2v2eλ2t,c1,c2∈R.

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

x(t)=c1[−21]et+c2[01]e−t,c1,c2∈R.

q-327974.name: Question 3
q-327974.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-6{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$
q-327974.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -6 & -3\end{aligned}].$

- Since $A$ is lower-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=-3\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=2.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -6 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -6\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

{x1′(t)=4x1(t)−x2(t)x2′(t)=2x1(t)+x2(t).

Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are λ1=3 and λ2=2.

b

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix A=[4−121].

  • Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

    • For λ1=3, we get A−λ1I=[1−12−2]∼[1−100]. So, we get an eigenvector v1=[11].

    • For λ2=2, we get A−λ2I=[2−12−1]∼[1−1200]. So, we get an eigenvector v2=[12].

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

q-39052.name: Question 5
q-39052.problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A.$ Find the decoupling matrix of the differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$
q-39052.worked_solution:
First, we construct the matrix $E$, whose columns are the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, the decoupling matrix can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={E}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\cdot (-3)-2\cdot (-4)}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-324455.name: Question 6
q-324455.problem:
Find the substitution that will decouple the following system of differential equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=3{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$
q-324455.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

- Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the eigenvalues are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=3\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=1.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we have $E=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the change of variables that decouples the system is given by $x(t)=Eu(t)$, or equivalently,

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t)={u}_{1}(t)-{u}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)={u}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Find the substitution that will decouple the following system of differential equations:

{x1′(t)=3x1(t)+2x2(t)x2′(t)=x2(t)

a
{x1(t)=u1(t)−u2(t)x2(t)=−u2(t)
b
{x1(t)=2u1(t)−u2(t)x2(t)=2u2(t)
c
{x1(t)=u1(t)+u2(t)x2(t)=u2(t)
d
{x1(t)=u1(t)−2u2(t)x2(t)=3u2(t)
e
{x1(t)=u1(t)−u2(t)x2(t)=u2(t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix A=[3201].

  • Since A is upper-triangular, the eigenvalues are λ1=3andλ2=1.

  • Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

    • For λ1=3, we get A−λ1I=[020−2]∼[0100]. So, we get an eigenvector v1=[10].

    • For λ2=1, we get A−λ2I=[2200]∼[1100]. So, we get an eigenvector v2=[−11].

Therefore, we have E=[1−101].

Finally, the change of variables that decouples the system is given by x(t)=Eu(t), or equivalently, {x1(t)=u1(t)−u2(t)x2(t)=u2(t).
